explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is an open-source CLI tool and Docker image providing a collection of Terraform/Terragrunt Git hooks.  
   - It plugs into the pre-commit framework, orchestrates checks (formatting, validation, security, docs, cost) via Python code and shell scripts, and can be consumed locally, in CI, or as a Docker container.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level:
     • src/pre_commit_terraform/ : Python package (CLI entrypoint, subcommands, parsing, error handling, structs).  
     • hooks/ : Bash wrapper scripts for each hook (terraform_fmt, terraform_validate, etc.).  
     • .pre-commit-hooks.yaml & .pre-commit-config.yaml (in readme) define hook IDs, entrypoints, args.  
     • Dockerfile & tools/entrypoint.sh : build and run container, set up user‐mapping.  
     • tests/ : unit tests for Python code and performance tests for hooks.  
     • .github/workflows/* : CI/CD pipelines for building, testing, releasing the image and Python package.  
     • pyproject.toml, hatch.toml, tox.ini, pytest.ini, and various linters’ configs: packaging, build, and static checks.

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Describes each hook’s purpose (terraform_fmt, terraform_docs, terraform_tflint, terraform_trivy, infracost_breakdown, etc.).  
   - Shows install options (local via pip, Docker), execution flows, environment variable overrides, and CI/CD examples on GitHub Actions.  
   - No existing architecture diagram—diagram will be a first-class deliverable.

4. How to create the system design diagram  
   a. Main components (boxes):  
     1. Developer Environment  
        - Git client + pre-commit framework  
        - Optional: Terraform/OpenTofu/Terragrunt/TFLint/Trivy/etc. binaries on PATH  
     2. Python CLI “pre_commit_terraform”  
        - Entry in src/__main__.py → _cli.py → _cli_subcommands.py  
        - Reads .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, dispatches to hooks  
     3. Hook Shell Scripts (hooks/*.sh)  
        - Common wrapper logic (_common.sh) + individual hook implementations  
     4. Docker Image  
        - Built from Dockerfile, installs Python CLI, hooks, and all external tools  
        - Entrypoint: tools/entrypoint.sh → pre-commit run  
     5. CI/CD (GitHub Actions)  
        - Builds Docker image, runs unit & integration tests, publishes package & image  
     6. External Services & Tools  
        - Terraform registry, Infracost API, container registry (GitHub Packages), GitHub API  
     7. Configuration & Metadata  
        - .pre-commit-hooks.yaml, hatch.toml, pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/*  

   b. Relationships and interactions (arrows):  
     - Developer makes a Git commit → pre-commit hook triggers → Python CLI invoked  
     - Python CLI loads hook metadata → calls corresponding shell script  
     - Shell script invokes external binary (terraform fmt/validate, tflint, tfsec/trivy, infracost, terrascan, tfupdate, hcledit)  
     - Results (exit code + stdout/stderr) returned upstream to pre-commit → commit allowed or blocked  
     - In Docker mode: local files bind-mounted into container → tools run inside container → results returned  
     - In CI (GitHub Actions): runner checks out code → container or Python package run pre-commit → upload status  

   c. Architectural patterns & design principles:  
     - Plugin/adapter pattern: each hook is a standalone script conforming to pre-commit’s interface  
     - Single-responsibility: Python code handles CLI parsing & orchestration; shell scripts handle individual tool invocation  
     - Containerization: Docker image encapsulates all runtime dependencies for consistency in CI  
     - Configuration-as-code: hooks defined declaratively in .pre-commit-hooks.yaml and .pre-commit-config.yaml  

   d. Key technologies, frameworks, libraries:  
     - Python 3.7+ (packaging via hatch, pyproject.toml)  
     - pre-commit framework  
     - Docker (Dockerfile, entrypoint.sh)  
     - Bash shell scripts (hooks/*.sh)  
     - Terraform / OpenTofu / Terragrunt / TFLint / Trivy / Checkov / Infracost / Terrascan / tfupdate / hcledit  
     - GitHub Actions for CI/CD  
     - Testing: pytest, shell tests, container-structure-test  

5. Tailoring the diagram for this open-source tool  
   - Emphasize core functionality (hook orchestration) rather than business domain flows.  
   - Show extensibility points: how new hooks (scripts) can be added, how hook metadata drives dispatch.  
   - Illustrate integration with external systems: Terraform registry, Infracost API, GitHub Packages.  
   - Depict dual execution modes: local binary vs. containerized.

6. Diagram guidelines  
   - Use clear rectangular boxes for components (group related files/directories inside).  
   - Draw directional arrows to show data/control flow:  
     • Git commit → pre-commit → Python CLI → hook script → external binary → back to CLI → pre-commit  
     • Docker build → Docker image → entrypoint → invoke same flow inside container  
     • CI pipeline triggers Docker build and test stages  
   - Color-code or shape-code by component type:  
     • Python code (blue boxes)  
     • Shell scripts (green boxes)  
     • External binaries/services (gray boxes)  
     • Configuration files (dotted-border boxes)  
     • CI/CD pipelines (purple box)  
   - Label all arrows with the protocol or file/event type (e.g., “exec”, “HTTP” for Infracost API, “bind-mount”, “git hook event”).

7. Emphasize detail without over-complicating  
   - Break the system into the maximum meaningful components listed above.  
   - Capture every essential interaction (Git → pre-commit → CLI → hooks → tools).  
   - Ensure each component is labeled, connections are directional, and color/shape distinguishes its type.

Use a standard diagramming tool (draw.io, Lucidchart, Visio, or PlantUML/C4) to lay out:

  [Developer Workstation]  
       │  
       ▼  
  [pre-commit framework]──reads──>[.pre-commit-hooks.yaml]  
       │  
       ▼  
  [pre_commit_terraform Python CLI]──invokes──>[hook script: terraform_fmt.sh]  
       │                                         ▲  
       ▼                                         │  
    … other hooks …                              │  
       │                                         │  
       ▼                                         │  
  [External Tool: terraform binary]              └─ common.sh library  
       │  
       ▼  
  Results → back to CLI → back to pre-commit → Git commit allowed/blocked  

Plus side panels for:

  • Docker Image (Dockerfile, entrypoint)  
  • CI/CD (GitHub Actions)  
  • External APIs (Infracost)  

Ensure all boxes, arrows, and labels reflect the specific directories, scripts, and workflows in this project.
